To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the performance of multithread TreadMarks is competitive with MPI; (ii) the performance of the multithreaded system is better than that of the original TreadMarks implementation; (iii) the multithread TreadsMarks system is simpler and more robust than the original Treadmarks implementation; and (iv) multithreaded OpenMP programs can be used on networks of SMPs
OpenMP can be efficiently implemented on a network of SMPs using a modified version of an SDSM system and the resulting performance of the multithreaded SDSM system is comparable to MPI.

(i) the multithreaded implementation of Tread Marks for SMPs is faster than the original implementation of the SDSM system and (ii) the multithreading approach achieves performance comparable with that of MPI for multithreaded applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of OpenMP for networks of SMPs.
the design and implementation of a system for parallel programming of networks of SMPs.
the development of a programming model for parallel computing that combines the advantages of shared memory with those of distributed memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OpenMP is a good programming model for networks of SMPs.
multithreading within a multiprocessors is a promising approach to parallel programming.
the multithreaded version of TreadMarks is a very effective implementation of OpenMP on a distributed-memory multiprocessor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OpenMP is an effective parallel programming model for SMP clusters and the multithreaded version of TreadMarks is a good implementation for it.
the OpenMP implementation for a network of SMPs achieves speedups comparable to MPI.
the performance of the OpenMP system is within 7?25% of the best possible speedup for each application, which is the performance of the MPI implementation on the same system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OpenMP model of parallel programming can be successfully applied to a cluster of SMPs.
OpenMP is a viable programming model for parallel programming on SMP clusters.
the OpenMP programming model is a viable approach for programming networks of shared-memory multipro- cessors.
